title: Britain, January 1929 - December 1936: the dollar-sterling rate, the Sauerbeck-Statist index and the cost of living, monthly
source: Bank of England, 'A millennium of macroeconomic data for the UK' (version 3.1): sheets 'M15. Mthly $-£ 1791-2015' and 'M6. Mthly prices and wages'
series: year, month; usd_per_gbp: dollars per pound (Craighead 2010, Federal Reserve Board and ONS); sauerbeck_1867_77_100: Sauerbeck-Statist index of all commodities, 1867-77 = 100, not seasonally adjusted; cost_of_living_jul1914_100: the ONS monthly cost of living index, July 1914 = 100
license: The workbook asks users to cite the underlying sources ('When using this data, please cite this source'). The Bank of England publishes it as a research dataset; a subset is stored here for teaching, with attribution to the Bank of England.
notes: Workbook SHA-256 4c23dd392a498691eac92659aec283fb43f28118bd80511dc87fc595974195eb. The same columns as Chapter 27's boe_millennium_interwar_monthly, which ends in December 1931. From April 1933 the dollar itself was off gold, so the rate after that month is no longer sterling's gold value.
citation: Bank of England, A Millennium of Macroeconomic Data for the UK, v3.1 (R. Thomas and N. Dimsdale, 2017), sheets M15 and M6
